2.1.summary: Both prototypes preserved byte-for-byte as immutable fixtures with a SHA-256 manifest; baseline reproduced on this Mac (counter 25 + Quick Quote 28 compiler tests; counter 4 and Quick Quote 4 Rust tests — Quick Quote only with its own target dir because both crates share a name; native and wasm32 library builds); KNOWN-BUG regressions pin the old defects (dynamic `@[click]` accepted, Rust Display numbers, tie-to-even toFixed, uncached computed).

2.2.summary: Machine-readable manifest generated from design §8: 126 inventory rows, 446 named entries (incl. 52 native tags), all 171 runtime exports of vue@3.5.43 classified (`isShallow` confirmed exported, 40 compiler-internal helpers flagged), Options API excluded, experimental APIs labelled E, default-deny lookup; plus a 465-entry closed-world standard-library/globals manifest. Tooling pair pinned and recorded: TypeScript 6.0.3 + vue-tsc 3.3.12 (@vue/language-core 3.3.12, @volar/typescript 2.4.28); TypeScript 7 is X for tooling because its package ships no JS compiler API (design §11 line 573, K07). A probe runs the pair programmatically on .vue files and reports versions read at run time.
2.2.evidence: `node --test "tests/profile/*.test.mjs"` (111 tests, incl. `typescript-pair.test.mjs` with negative controls for wrong installed versions and range pins); `node tooling/manifest/build-manifest.mjs --check`; `node tooling/types/probe.mjs`; artifacts `compiler/profile/{manifest.json,stdlib.json}`, `compiler/types/pair.mjs`, `docs/compatibility/`, `docs/evidence/typescript-tooling.md`.

2.3.summary: Untrusted build steps run under a deny-default macOS `sandbox-exec` profile (workspace-only writes, no network, no inherited env); hostile npm-postinstall-style and Cargo build.rs-style fixtures prove the sentinel secret, outside writes and network are blocked while the same attacks succeed unsandboxed; dependency policy and a candidate-obligation ledger exist (13 of 15 entries honestly 'unresolved'). Limits documented: sandbox-exec is deprecated/best-effort, containers and VMs not verified.

3.1.summary: The real AOT path (JS/TS → HIR → Rust over the managed `vn-value` runtime, no interpreter or eval) matches Node/V8 on 79 language and 166 lowering scenarios, natively and on wasm32. A selected Test262 subset (307 files from upstream 2e0a567, chosen by coded rules, BSD license vendored) gives 232 pass, 0 fail, 75 rejected by the profile, each listed. A release size and allocation report covers Counter and Quick Quote: headless native about 2.9–3.1 MB stripped, web app wasm about 1.4–1.5 MB raw (461–485 KB gzip), host wasm 46 KB; peak live heap 950 and 2,070 objects for the two interaction scripts.
3.1.evidence: `node tooling/harness/run-test262.mjs` (232/0/75; ledger `tests/language/test262/status.json`; control `--dir tests/language/test262/controls --no-ledger` fails as required); `node tooling/report/aot-size.mjs [--json]`; `node --test "tests/tooling/**/*.test.mjs"`; artifacts `docs/evidence/aot-size-report.md`, `docs/evidence/test262-subset.md`.
3.1.missing: Cost comparison against an engine-backed alternative (no engine-backed variant built; no sourced size figure for QuickJS/Boa in the repo).

3.2.summary: Non-moving generation-checked heap with iterative mark-sweep at safepoints. A churn workload (lists, cycles, wide objects, Maps, closures, a stable live set, persistent roots) is checked after every collection against an independent reachability model, with steady heap size and two negative controls. Pause benchmark (one release run, 4 vCPU container): p99 6.8 ms at 10k live objects, 16.5 ms at 100k, 206 ms at 1M, so the collector MISSES the design §14 2 ms p99 slice budget at every size. A standalone gc-arena 0.7.0 experiment with the same shape also misses 2 ms at 1M and is not recommended (see 3.8). Miri/ASan: not applicable, both crates `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.
3.2.evidence: `cargo test -p vn-value --test gc_churn --test gc_exhaustion`; `cargo run --release -p vn-value --example gc_churn_bench`; `experiments/heap/gc-arena-churn/` (`cargo run --release`, own workspace); artifact `docs/evidence/gc-latency.md`.

3.3.summary: Exact Vue 3.5 scheduler, watchers, nextTick and effect graph match real vue@3.5.43 (115/115 V0 scenarios; 403 random promise programs match V8 job ordering). Scope-owned operations carry (owner slot, generation, operation id): stopping the owning scope asks the host to cancel and discards late completions without running user callbacks; an explicit cancel by a live owner rejects with a Cancelled ServiceError; ordinary promises keep JS behaviour; a recreated component never receives an old instance's delivery.
3.3.evidence: `node tooling/harness/run-language.mjs --with-vue` (115/115); `cargo test -p vn-runtime --test owned_operations` (12 tests incl. unmount-during-request, stale generation and both cancel/complete race orders; mutation runs recorded); oracle `tests/vue/owned-ops/record.mjs`; artifact `docs/evidence/scope-cancellation.md`.

3.4.missing: Everything in the task: renderer comparison, layout/hit testing, focus, bidi text, AT actions, license costing.

3.5.summary: Needs real iPhone/iPad and Android devices with VoiceOver/TalkBack and IME; none are available here (iOS simulators exist, Android has no NDK/JDK). A simulator alone cannot pass this gate.

3.6.summary: Rust/WASM DOM boundary proven in headless Chrome (`WebHost`, 45 imports). SSR/hydration probe on the headless DocHost: Rust SSR output is byte-identical to @vue/server-renderer 3.5.43 renderToString for 17 oracle cases (escaping, fragment and v-if anchors, keyed lists, attributes, v-model value); two interleaved realms keep separate state; createSSRApp hydration adopts the server nodes with no creations; a text input edited before hydration keeps the edit (Vue 3.5.43 behaviour); text/tag/extra/missing mismatches are repaired and logged; Teleport/Transition/KeepAlive/Suspense/async components throw.
3.6.evidence: `cargo test -p vn-runtime --test ssr_hydration` (21 tests); `node tests/ssr-oracle/probe.mjs`; `node --test "tests/platform/web/*.test.mjs"` (CI, Chrome); artifact `docs/evidence/ssr-hydration-probe.md`.
3.6.missing: Hydration in the browser (WebHost lacks first_child/node_type/node_value; needs an ABI decision), three-engine browser run, hydration payload schema-hash validation, and a decision on checkbox/radio/select edits before hydration (Vue resets them to the model; design §13 says edits are adopted).

3.7.summary: Tooling pair pinned (TypeScript 6.0.3 + vue-tsc 3.3.12; TS 7 excluded). An uncaught throw, including one after an await, is reported with `.vue` file:line:col frames (emitter source sites for functions, throw statements and await resumption points; error.stack unchanged). `vue-native dev` (headless) rebuilds on change and restarts with a JSON-lines state snapshot of root script-setup refs; closures, host handles, Maps/Sets and computed refs are not serialized. Edit-to-ready over 10 edits (dev profile, types on): Counter p50 1.5 s, Quick Quote p50 2.2 s, within the design's 5 s build budget for these small apps.
3.7.missing: Editor/LSP behaviour (virtual-file editor fixtures), frames for runtime-raised errors and synchronous call sites, web-target dev loop, the 100-SFC latency fixture and a release-profile comparison.

3.8.summary: Draft G1/G2 decision record written: G1 fails on collector latency only (semantics pass every oracle), G2 is not evaluable without 3.4 and 3.5. It recommends narrowing the G1 claim to a stated live-heap ceiling and making incremental collection the next runtime package, and keeping slice claims to web DOM + headless until hardware exists.
3.8.missing: Owner sign-off on the recommendations; 3.4 and 3.5 evidence; a named reference workload for the 2 ms budget.

4.1.summary: Source-located versioned HIR (`hirVersion: 1`), checked emitter, identifier mangling and diagnostics with `.vue`-mapped spans replace the prototype's direct string emission. The prototype's `@[click]` defect has an explicit regression test through the new pipeline: an undeclared name is rejected with a spanned VN4016, and a declared one binds the handler under the runtime event name (checked headless; the prototype output fails both assertions). Dynamic argument names are now checked for every directive. The HIR schema (69 node kinds, 16 records) has a committed sha256 and a walker checks every lowering fixture against it.

4.2.summary: Primitive math/strings/booleans, mutable captured aliases and JS decimal formatting execute correctly natively and on wasm32 with automatic GC roots: the same generated scenario modules run as a wasm32-unknown-unknown cdylib against the same Node goldens, byte-identical to native, also with a collection at every safepoint. Deep recursion needed an 8 MiB wasm shadow stack.
4.2.evidence: `node tooling/harness/run-language-wasm.mjs` (79/79) and `--dir tests/language/lowering` (166/166), also `--gc-threshold 1`; `node --test tests/language/wasm.test.mjs` (subset with mutated-golden and trap controls); `cargo test -p vn-testkit --test wasm_entry`; artifact `docs/evidence/wasm-execution.md`.

4.3.summary: Components with props/emits, keyed children and unmount run through the real renderer on DocHost. Acceptance tests show: two instances of one component stay independent; a computed read twice evaluates once; removing a keyed child stops its watcher and releases its effects, computed, scope, listener and subscriber edges; 50 unmount/recreate cycles of 20 children return effects, computeds, scopes, watchers, deps, links, subscriber edges, host handles, listeners and GC live objects to a measured baseline. Unmount ordering is recorded from vue@3.5.43; leaking variants are negative controls.
4.3.evidence: `cargo test -p vn-runtime --test ownership` (11 tests); oracle `tests/ownership-oracle/record.mjs`; `node tooling/harness/run-language.mjs --with-vue --ui` (174/174, also `--gc-stress`); artifact `docs/evidence/component-ownership.md`.

5.5.summary: Static ESM across multiple files, live bindings, cycles, re-exports, namespace objects, native module imports and `.vue` imports compile and run. Literal `import()` (string or no-substitution template) joins the prelinked project graph, defers the target's first evaluation, resolves to the shared namespace, evaluates once and caches rejections; settlement runs on host turns that start when the promise job queue is empty, matched to the Node project oracle. Computed specifiers (VN2019), import options (new VN2031) and unresolvable or native targets are rejected at compile time with spans.
5.5.evidence: `node tooling/harness/run-projects.mjs` (14/14, incl. dyn-basic, dyn-throw, dyn-cycle, dyn-order); `cargo test -p vn-value --test modules_dynamic` (10 tests); `node --test tests/compiler/project/dynamic.test.mjs`; artifact `docs/evidence/dynamic-import.md`.
5.5.missing: Dynamic import on the web target (no browser run), chunk graph output, and calibration of several cases (repeated requests of one module, cycles among unloaded modules, link errors of unloaded targets). Settlement timing follows the hook-based project oracle, not plain Node.

5.6.summary: Heap limit and execution-budget watchdogs, GC safepoint discipline and stress tests. Long churn keeps async/module/effect roots correct against an independent model with steady heap size; exceeding the heap limit mid-churn is a catchable RangeError (no panic) and the runtime is usable afterwards; host handles registered under an effect scope close exactly once on stop, never while the scope is live across GC, and close callbacks run with the heap open. Allocation and pause tails are reported (they miss the 2 ms budget; see 3.2). Miri/ASan/FFI audit: not applicable, `vn-value` and `vn-runtime` forbid unsafe code.
5.6.evidence: `cargo test -p vn-value --test gc_churn --test gc_exhaustion`; `cargo test -p vn-runtime --test realm_scope_handles` (9 tests; mutation runs recorded); `cargo run --release -p vn-value --example gc_churn_bench`; artifact `docs/evidence/gc-latency.md`.

5.7.summary: SFC frontend wraps the official compileScript/compileTemplate/compileStyle with profile checks, native template validation and `.vue` spans; macros come from Vue itself; TypeScript is erased at lowering. `vue-native check` type-checks .vue/.ts modules with the pinned TypeScript 6.0.3 + vue-tsc 3.3.12 pair (VN7001 at .vue spans; `--no-types` skips it). Imported prop types resolve through compileScript with an fs adapter rooted at the project; type imports a macro reads but compileScript cannot resolve (bare packages, names a file does not export) are VN6017 in build too. TS-only runtime constructs (enum, namespace, using) stay rejected with the checker on.
5.7.evidence: `node --test tests/compiler/types/check.test.mjs tests/compiler/sfc/imported-types.test.mjs tests/cli/check-types.test.mjs`; `node tooling/harness/check-sfc-lowering.mjs` (45/45); `node tooling/cli/vue-native.mjs check examples/quick-quote`; artifact `docs/evidence/typescript-tooling.md`.
